note.text:
Mass is measured with a balance, in kilograms (kg) or grams (g): 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 g = 1000 mg. In the laboratory we use a top-pan (electronic) balance. Put the empty container on first and press “zero” (tare), then add the substance: the screen shows only the substance's mass.
Volume of a liquid is measured in cm³ or mL (1 cm³ = 1 mL; 1 L = 1000 cm³):
• measuring cylinder for most volumes;
• pipette or burette when the volume must be exact.
Read the bottom of the meniscus with your eye level with it.

worked_example.problem: A beaker has a mass of {b} g. With salt in it, the mass is {t} g. What is the mass of the salt?
steps: Mass of the salt = mass with salt − mass of the empty beaker.
(With a tare button, set the empty beaker to zero and read the salt directly.)

cards.idea: Mass: use a balance. 1 kg = {factor('kg', 'g')} g, 1 g = {factor('g', 'mg')} mg.
example: A packet of {m} g of salt has a mass of {convertUnit(m, 'g', 'kg')} kg.

cards.idea: Weighing by difference: mass of substance = (container + substance) − container. Or press “zero” with the empty container on.
example: Empty dish {a} g; dish with sugar {b} g; sugar {b - a} g.

cards.idea: Volume of a liquid: read the bottom of the meniscus in a measuring cylinder. 1 L = {factor('L', 'cm³')} cm³ and 1 mL = 1 cm³.

questions.prompt: Convert this mass: {up ? k / 10 : k * 10} {up ? p.a : p.b} = ? {up ? p.b : p.a}
questions.answer: up ? convertUnit(k / 10, p.a, p.b) : convertUnit(k * 10, p.b, p.a)

misconceptions.wrong: up ? convertUnit(k / 10, p.b, p.a) : convertUnit(k * 10, p.a, p.b)
misconceptions.explain: You went the wrong way: to a smaller unit the number gets bigger.

questions.prompt: An empty beaker has a mass of {a / 10} g. With copper(II) sulfate crystals in it, the mass is {(a + s) / 10} g. What is the mass of the crystals?

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the empty beaker from the total; do not add.

questions.prompt: What volume of water is in the measuring cylinder, in cm³?

misconceptions.explain: Read at the bottom of the curved surface (the meniscus).

questions.hint: Each small mark is {step} cm³. Look at the bottom of the curve.
solution: The bottom of the meniscus is on {answer} cm³.

questions.prompt: Convert this volume: {up ? k / 10 : k * 10} {up ? p.a : p.b} = ? {up ? p.b : p.a}
questions.answer: up ? convertUnit(k / 10, p.a, p.b) : convertUnit(k * 10, p.b, p.a)

misconceptions.wrong: up ? convertUnit(k / 10, p.b, p.a) : convertUnit(k * 10, p.a, p.b)
misconceptions.explain: You went the wrong way: to a smaller unit the number gets bigger.

questions.prompt: Tabe pours {a} cm³ of water and then {b} cm³ of dilute acid into a beaker. What volume of liquid is in the beaker, in cm³?

misconceptions.explain: Both liquids are in the beaker: add the volumes.

questions.prompt: One result is worked out wrongly. Which one?

right.text: Empty beaker {a} g, beaker with salt {a + s} g: the salt is {s} g.

wrong.text: Empty beaker {b} g, beaker with sugar {b + t} g: the sugar is {2 * b + t} g.
